title: A Phase 3 Relapse Prevention Trial Evaluating KarXT Treatment in Schizophrenia
official: A Phase 3 Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Randomized Withdrawal Maintenance Trial of KarXT Treatment in Participants with Schizophrenia
summary: Main objective: To find out whether KarXT works better than a placebo (a pill with no active medicine) to prevent schizophrenia symptoms from getting worse again (called relapse) after a person’s symptoms have become stable.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participants must be between 18 to 65 years of age.
2. They must have a primary diagnosis of schizophrenia for at least 1 year.
3. They must have experienced hospitalization for schizophrenia within 1 year.
4. Participants must be experiencing residual schizophrenia symptoms.
5. They need to meet a minimum score on two important assessments that ask about the seriousness of schizophrenia symptoms.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participants are not allowed to have any other diagnosis other than schizophrenia.
2. They are also not allowed to be experiencing moderate to severe substance use disorder within the last year.
3. Individuals will be excluded from the study if they fail a urine drug screen or alcohol test when they come in for screening.
4. Individuals who have thoughts of wanting to hurt themselves or someone else.
5. Participants who have a history of glaucoma.
6. Participants who experience bowel difficulties or difficulty urinating.
7. Pregnant or breastfeeding women will be excluded.
